To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an efficient, fully probabilistic method for nonlinear Bayesian inversion of geophysical data.

(a) a new, rapid, and scalable inversion method has been developed for the spatial distribution of rock properties; (b) the method is fully probabilistic, deterministic, and scalable to large models; (c) the method can incorporate prior knowledge about geological parameters, and (d) the method is robust to noise present in geophysical data as long as the noise statistics are known.

(1) a discriminative approach to probabilistic inversion can reduce the modeling effort significantly; (2) a variational Bayes approach to inference provides a scalable alternative to Markov chain Monte-Carlo based inference; and (3) the method honors spatial distributions supplied as prior information and can be trained to be robust against noisy data.

developing a new probabilistic inversion method that can be used to estimate the spatially distributed geological properties from geophysical data in a fully probabilistic and scalable way.
